title: High Expressive Ratio

location.series: COLLINS / San Francisco Symphony case study
location.extent: Whole published artwork or representative frame of complete local clip

slide_intent: Bound a variable type treatment because expressive range must retain enough recognizable structure to be useful.
strategic_value: A controlled italic range can give the Symphony variety without abandoning the serif letter’s identity.
demonstration: A row of E specimens marks 100%, 110%, 120%, 130% and 140% as variable italics inside an orange Goldilocks Zone; pale outer examples are labeled No backslant and Too slanted.
practical_value: Use the demonstrated 100–140% interval for this italic specimen without converting its percentages into angles.

content_islands.name: Accepted range
content_islands.spec: Place the five dark E specimens and printed percentage labels inside the orange boundary.

content_islands.name: Excluded extremes
content_islands.spec: Keep the pale backslanted specimen at left and excessive slants at right with their captions.

reference_purposes.Expression: A row of E specimens marks 100%, 110%, 120%, 130% and 140% as variable italics inside an orange Goldilocks Zone; pale outer examples are labeled No backslant and Too slanted.

reference_purposes.Intent: The accompanying High Expressive Ratio text describes generating expressive range from minimal elements.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The specimen brackets 100–140% as the variable-italic range and labels outer examples No backslant and Too slanted; these are the printed specimen units, not degrees.
